surtitre: Deploying a core model, site by site
titre: An SAP roll-out approach, from A to Z
intro: Click a bar, a gate or the go-live to open the details.
chronologieAria: Roll-out timeline: phases, steps and gates from M-8 to M+2
causesTitre: The 5 most common causes of failure
note: Generic approach with indicative durations, to be adapted to the program's method.

s1.s: Which sites, in what order, with which resources
s1.obj: Decide which sites move onto the core model, in what order and with which resources.
act: Blackout periods: closings, peak activity, holidays
pre: Core model stable and live on at least one site
Roll-out governance in place: committees, design authority, change board
ai: Analyze site data (volumes, materials, complexity) to rank sites and form waves
Simulate several wave plans and their load on the team
s1.ex: Nordval has six sites to deploy. Lyon, the pilot site, has been running on the core model for six months. Porto is chosen for wave 2: mid-sized, with processes close to Lyon's. Mexico, more complex, goes in wave 3. Target go-live is March 15: December is ruled out because of the annual closing, summer because of holidays.
s1.own: Client program management, with the integrator
r: Core model still unstable: every site pays for the fixes
Freeze one core model version per wave
Overly ambitious waves, several large sites in parallel: team saturated
Limit parallel sites, start with a simple pilot
Business calendar ignored: go-live in the middle of a closing
Build the blackout periods into the plan from day one

s2.s: Is the site ready, criterion by criterion?
s2.obj: Measure whether the site can receive the solution: processes, data, infrastructure, people, interfaces, cutover constraints.
act: Rating each criterion green, amber or red
Action plan with an owner and a date for each action
pre: Standard assessment grid for the program
Site counterparts named: site director, local process owners
Access to the site's data and infrastructure
ai: Pre-fill the grid from site extracts: data quality, volumes
Process mining (e.g. SAP Signavio): see how the site really works, not what it says
s2.ex: Three days on site. Processes: green. Data: amber, 18% of materials have no packaging unit. Infrastructure: red, no WiFi in the outdoor storage area. People: amber, a single key user for three processes. Actions: WiFi audit before end of October (Porto IT), two more key users named by the site director.
r: Self-declared assessment, 'everything is fine': surprises at build
Verify with evidence: data extracts, real WiFi test
Actions with no owner or date: they stay red until go-live
Track every action in committee
Site barely involved, then unavailable
Have the site director sign the report

s3.s: Core model versus site: adopt, adapt, refuse
s3.obj: Compare how the site works against the core model and decide on each gap.
act: Fit-to-standard workshops with local key users, demonstration of the core model
List of gaps: legal, business, organizational
Decision per gap: standard, configuration, development or refusal
Design authority or change board review for gaps that touch the core model
pre: Core model documented: processes, configuration, developments
Site key users available and empowered to decide
Rules for handling gaps: who decides what
ai: Compare the site's actual processes to the core model and pre-classify gaps
Check whether a similar gap has already been handled at another site
s3.ex: Four workshops, eleven gaps. Portuguese customs labels are mandatory: gap accepted, a form will be developed. The site wants to keep its color-based bin marking: refused, standard EWM does the same thing differently. A putaway rule Porto proposes for all sites goes to the design authority. Result: six accepted, four refused, one under arbitration.
r: The site recreates its old way of working through gaps: custom code explodes
Require a legal or quantified justification for every gap
Gaps discovered only at acceptance: delays
Work processes end to end, not just screens
Local gap pushed into the core model without arbitration: regression on other sites
Mandatory design authority review

s4.s: Scope, schedule, budget and team locked
s4.obj: Lock the site's scope, schedule, budget and team.
act: Estimating deltas, data, testing and training
Detailed schedule with milestones and gates
ai: Estimating assisted by the history of previous sites
Spot tasks in the schedule that were underestimated compared to past sites
s4.ex: Estimate: 180 days for the six gaps, 60 for data, 90 for testing, 40 for training. Seven-month schedule up to March 15. The supplier signs its commitment on the six validated gaps only; the gap at the design authority is provisioned separately.
r: Estimating on gaps that are still vague: drift
Estimate only mature gaps, provision for the rest
Schedule that squeezes testing to hit the date: bugs in production
Protect testing duration in the schedule
Supplier commitment signed before gaps are validated: the supplier absorbs the cost
Make the commitment conditional on the validated baseline

g1.obj: Authorize the move into Adjust: the site is understood, the scope locked, the plan funded.
act: Review of the readiness report and action plan
pre: No blocking red in the SRA, or a credible plan to clear it
liv: Traced go-ahead decision, with its conditions
ai: Automatically consolidate the status of the gate criteria
g1.ex: The committee authorizes the move into Adjust with one condition: the WiFi, still red, has a funded action plan and will be reviewed at gate 2.
r: Gate passed 'with conditions' but the conditions are never followed up
Each condition has an owner, a date and committee follow-up

s5.obj: Adapt the solution to the site.
act: Configuring the site organization: company, plant, warehouse, bins
pre: Development environments and transport route available
liv: Configuration and developments delivered to quality
ai: Draft specifications from the gap register
ABAP code generation and review (e.g. Joule for developers)
s5.ex: The PT01 warehouse is configured: 2,400 bins. The customs form and the interface with the local carrier are developed. The carrier delivers its specifications three weeks late: the risk is raised in committee on day one.
r: Specifications that change during the build: delay and overrun
Every change goes through the change board
Double maintenance with core model changes: conflicts
Organized transport calendar and retrofit
Local interface depends on a third party: blocked
Identify the third party and its schedule from Diagnose

s6.obj: Migrate correct and complete data within the time available.
act: Cleansing data in the legacy system
Two to three mock loads with business checks
Measuring reject rate and load time
liv: Load duration measured and carried into the runbook
ai: Detect duplicates, anomalies and inconsistent fields in the source data
Propose mapping rules
Automatically check each mock load
s6.ex: Mock load 1: 22% rejects, mostly missing packaging units and duplicate bins. The data owner launches the cleansing. Mock load 2: 4% rejects. Mock load 3: 0.5%, load time 5h40, for an 8-hour cutover window.
s6.own: Client data owners and migration team
r: Cleansing started too late: dirty data at go-live
Start from Diagnose, with a quality threshold per mock load
Token business validation: errors found in production
The data owner signs each mock load
Load duration unknown: cutover exceeds the window
Time every mock load

act: Network and WiFi coverage, including storage areas
Workstations, mobile terminals, scanners, label printers
pre: Budget and purchase lead times known
ai: Analyze WiFi coverage surveys and spot risk areas
Generate authorization lists by role
s7.ex: The audit finds two dead zones in the outdoor storage: six WiFi access points added. 45 terminals and 8 label printers ordered in October, delivered in January.
r: Equipment purchase lead time underestimated: blocking at go-live
Order as soon as the baseline is set
WiFi coverage never tested in real conditions: warehouse operators blocked
Test coverage zone by zone
Authorizations created the day before: users without access
Create them before acceptance and test them

s8.obj: Verify that processes work end to end, interfaces included.
act: End-to-end scenarios: receiving, storage, picking, shipping
pre: Realistic test data from a mock load
ai: Generate test scenarios and datasets from the processes
Analyze, classify and deduplicate defects
s8.ex: 64 end-to-end scenarios, 37 defects, 3 of them blocking. Example: the carrier interface rejects deliveries of more than 99 parcels. Fixed in two weeks. Exit: zero blocking, two major with a workaround.
r: Incomplete or shared environment: testing blocked
Reserve the environment and the third-party systems
Unrealistic test data: bugs in production
Test on data from a mock load
Vague exit criteria: testing drags on
Set the exit criteria before starting

s9.s: Validation by the site, without breaking the others
s9.obj: Have the site's users validate the solution without degrading the sites already in production.
act: Acceptance by key users on their real cases
pre: Integration testing finished according to its criteria
Key users available and trained on the test tool
Up-to-date regression set, automated where possible
ai: Automate regression (e.g. Tricentis)
Summarize acceptance feedback and spot out-of-scope requests
s9.ex: Six key users test for three weeks. Fourteen comments, including five new requests sent to the change board, two accepted for a later release. Regression on Lyon: 320 automated tests, all green. The site director signs the acceptance.
r: Key users tied up in their day job: rushed acceptance
Reserve their time in the schedule, with the site director's agreement
Acceptance turns into a list of new requests: drift
Requests go to the change board, not into acceptance
Regression neglected: outage on a site already in production
Make the set mandatory and automate it

g2.obj: Authorize the move into Deploy: the solution is tested, the data and the site are ready.
pre: Zero blocking defects, major defects with a workaround
Mock loads within quality and duration thresholds
ai: Consolidate the status of defects, mock loads and infrastructure
g2.ex: Zero blocking defects, mock loads within thresholds, WiFi turned green. Move into Deploy authorized.
r: Defects downgraded to 'minor' to pass the gate
Severity arbitrated by the business, not by the team delivering

s10.s: Users able to work from day 1
s10.obj: Make every user able to work from the first day.
act: End-user training on a dedicated environment
liv: Trained users, with an attendance rate
ai: Generate work instructions, materials and quizzes by role
Translate materials for foreign sites
s10.ex: Four key users trained as trainers. The 40 warehouse operators are trained in three sessions, three weeks before go-live, on real cases: receiving a truck, picking an urgent order. Attendance: 95%.
r: Training too early: forgotten by go-live
Train two to four weeks before
Training on the tool but not on the new process: errors
Train by business scenario
Resistance not addressed, managers absent: workarounds
Involve the site's managers

s11.obj: Prepare the cutover minute by minute, then rehearse it.
act: Point of no return and fallback plan
pre: Cutover window validated with the business
ai: Check runbook consistency: dependencies, durations, forgotten tasks
Compare with the runbooks of previous sites
s11.ex: Runbook of 186 tasks. Cutover from Friday 6 pm to Sunday 6 pm. Rehearsal three weeks before: 9h10 instead of the planned 8 hours, so two tasks are parallelized. Point of no return: Saturday 2 pm. Full physical inventory on Friday.
r: No rehearsal: the real cutover overruns the window
At least one complete, timed rehearsal
Fallback never tested: unusable on D-day
Test it during the rehearsal
Physical stock differs from system stock: wrong data from day 1
Take inventory before the cutover

s12.obj: Decide, on criteria written in advance, whether to cut over.
act: Review of criteria: testing, data, training, infrastructure, support, runbook
pre: Go / no-go criteria defined and signed in advance
ai: Prepare the criteria dashboard
s12.ex: Wednesday committee: 14 criteria green, 1 amber, two key users on leave the first week. Decision: go with a reservation, a consultant from Lyon comes as reinforcement.
r: Pressure of the date: go despite red criteria
Criteria set in advance and not renegotiable in the meeting
Reservations not followed after the go: incidents
Each reservation has an owner and a date
No-go seen as a failure: nobody dares propose it
Present it as a normal steering option

s13.s: Execute the runbook, open the site
s13.obj: Execute the cutover and start operations on the new solution.
act: Opening to users, first flows under watch
ai: Monitor failing flows and reconciliation gaps in real time
s13.ex: The old software stops Friday at 6 pm. Inventory, load, reconciliation: gap of 12 items out of 12,000, corrected before opening. Opening Sunday at 4 pm, first truck received Monday at 6 am.
r: Forgotten task or poorly managed dependency: chain delay
Hourly checkpoints on the runbook
Reconciliation skipped to save time: invisible stock gaps
Reconciliation mandatory before opening
Fallback decided too late: neither the old nor the new system
Fallback criteria set before the point of no return

s14.obj: Stabilize the site during the first weeks in production.
act: Tracking indicators: incidents, failing flows, lead times
ai: Triage and classify tickets
Suggest solutions from already-resolved incidents
Spot trends before they become crises
s14.ex: Four weeks of hypercare. Week 1: 85 tickets, 60% of them usage questions. Week 4: 9 tickets. Exit criterion: fewer than 10 tickets a week and no blocking incident for two weeks.
r: Experts leave too early for the next site: incidents unanswered
Lock the hypercare team until exit
Endless hypercare: cost and confusion with run
Quantified exit criteria
Unreported workarounds: hidden problems
Presence on the floor, listening to users

s15.t: Handover to run and lessons learned
s15.s: Hand over, improve the next wave
s15.obj: Hand maintenance over to run and improve the following waves.
act: Knowledge transfer and documentation to run
Updating the core model and the method
ai: Produce documentation for run
Synthesize lessons learned from all sites
s15.ex: Two weeks of shadowing with the run team. Lessons learned: the first mock load came too late, and the WiFi should have been audited from scoping. Both points are added to the SRA grid for Mexico.
r: Handover without documentation: run still depends on the project team
Shadowing, then reverse shadowing, before releasing the team
Lessons learned never done: same mistakes in the next wave
Mandatory workshop before the next site, with tracked actions

g3.obj: Close the site project and confirm that run can take over alone.
act: Review of the handover to run
pre: Indicators below thresholds for an agreed period
ai: Calculate stability indicators over the period
g3.ex: Hypercare exit declared six weeks after go-live. Three minor tickets are formally taken over by run.
r: Closure declared with incidents still open: run inherits a debt
List of open incidents formally taken over by run

transverse.obj: Run the roll-out end to end: decide fast, arbitrate cleanly, keep the site engaged.
act: Steering committee: arbitration, gates, go / no-go
Design authority: compliance with the core model
Change board: every change to scope, schedule or budget
Change management and communication towards the site
pre: Roles and bodies defined from scoping
ai: Committee minutes and decision tracking
Early risk detection from indicators
Caution: client data only in a tool approved by the client
transverse.ex: Monthly steering committee, then weekly for the last six weeks. The register tracks 14 risks; only the carrier delay and the WiFi turned red, and both were handled before gate 2.
r: Committees that observe without deciding: problems pile up
Every committee ends with traced decisions
Indicators green, reality red: the watermelon effect
Quantified alert thresholds and checks on the ground
Site sponsor absent: arbitration blocked
Have them sit on the site's gates
